creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`muster pane new --run X --name Y` whose split answer misses the 500ms deadline exits 4, and the pane herdr made is left a bare shell: no command typed, no label. `HerdrBackend::equip`, which types the command and sets the label, runs only after an answer that arrived in time.

This predates 2026-09-13. Since `a_2P65ttmCu` the late answer is read on a thread of its own and binds the pane's name, so that thread now holds everything `equip` needs.

It matters most under load, which is when splits time out, and `muster pane new --run` is how parallel-work rounds start their worker agents. The result is a pane with no agent in it and a caller told exit 4.

The decision this card is for: should the late-answer thread run the command and set the label? For: the caller asked for it, and exit 4 means "may have happened". Against: a command starting seconds after the caller was told the request went unanswered, and a caller that retried despite exit 4 would get two agents.

Found by the integrator reviewing slot 1's work in the 2026-09-13 round.
title: A pane new --run whose split timed out never runs its command or takes its --name
